about.title: We're from here, and it shows
about.lead: Adrenalina Cabo operates at Playa Migriño, between the Baja desert and the open Pacific. We work with small groups because an adventure lands differently when your guide remembers your name.
about.missionBody: That everyone who rides with us goes home telling a story they didn't expect. That only happens when the team is well looked after, the safety gear is in order and nobody is in a hurry.
about.visionBody: We want to be the operation people recommend by name, not by price. To grow without losing what sets us apart: small groups, local staff and dealing with us directly.

values.title: Safety before anything
values.body: Certified bilingual guides, equipment checked before every departure, and medical service with an ambulance available 24 hours. If conditions aren't safe, we don't ride.

values.title: Animal welfare
values.body: Our camels and horses live in a sanctuary registered with SEMARNAT, with scheduled rest and weight limits we actually enforce.

values.title: Local people, local jobs
values.body: The team is from around here. Guides, mechanics, handlers and kitchen staff, all from Los Cabos and La Paz.

values.title: Pricing without tricks
values.body: Park entrance and insurance are inside the published price. We charge nothing extra when you arrive.

reviews.title: Why do our clients love us?

items.text: We booked the ATV tour and it was the highlight of the trip. Our guide walked us through everything calmly, the scenery is unreal, and we never felt rushed.
items.author: Jessica M.

items.text: We came with two kids and thought it would be complicated. The UTV was perfect and the camels blew their minds. Zero hidden costs, everything exactly as promised.
items.author: Carlos R.

items.text: We arrived on a cruise with a tight window and they still fit us in. Picked us up on time and got us back to the ship with room to spare. Highly recommend.
items.author: Mark T.

items.a: We run fixed departures at 9:00, 10:00, 12:00, 13:00, 15:00 and 16:00. In high season we add 8:00 and 17:00. We confirm your time when you book.

items.q: Where are you and how do I get there?
items.a: We're at Playa Migriño, Carretera Federal 19 km 100, about 30 minutes from downtown Cabo San Lucas. Round-trip transportation from your hotel is already included.

items.q: What's included in the price and what's paid separately?
items.a: The tour price includes round-trip transportation from your hotel, safety equipment, a bilingual guide, the ecological hike, desert safari, lockers, water, tacos and quesadillas, and a tequila tasting. Paid separately: the park entrance fee ($25 USD per person, mandatory on every tour) and, if you want them, vehicle protection and the photo package.
To drive an ATV or UTV you must be 16 with photo ID. As a passenger, 7 years on an ATV and 5 on a UTV. Mini RZR from age 10 to drive. Camels from 5, horses from 6, and Sky Bike from 8.

items.q: Are there weight or height limits?
items.a: Yes. ATV and UTV: 125 kg maximum, minimum height 1.20 m. Horses: 110 kg maximum. Sky Bike: 120 kg maximum and 1.20 m minimum height.
Pregnant guests, anyone with back or neck problems, recent surgeries, or under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Your safety comes first.
Comfortable clothes you don't mind getting dusty, closed shoes, sunscreen, a light sweater and a hands-free camera. We provide the helmet and goggles, and lockers are free.

items.q: Can I swim at the beach?
items.a: No. Migriño is open Pacific with very strong currents and is not safe for swimming. The beach is for riding, and that rule isn't negotiable.

items.q: Is there food at the park?
items.a: Yes. We have a cafeteria with healthy food, a fast-food area, vegan options and a bar. There's also the Beach Club, with à la carte meals. With the Day Pass, food is included.

items.q: Can I cancel or change my booking?
items.a: Yes, with no penalty up to 48 hours before your tour if you paid in full. If you booked with a deposit, the window is 72 hours. Under that, or a no-show, is non-refundable. If we cancel for weather, we reschedule or refund you in full.
We accept Visa, Mastercard and American Express online. You can also pay a deposit now and the balance on arrival.

items.q: Is there a discount for locals?
items.a: Yes, 30% off. If you live in Baja California Sur, show ID with your address and get the local rate. Message us on WhatsApp and we'll confirm it.

items.q: Can someone come along without taking the tour?
items.a: Yes, but they also pay the $25 USD park entrance fee. That covers the common areas and the Beach Club while they wait for you.

atv.name: ATVs
atv.tagline: The Migriño classic, on your own machine
atv.intro:
Two routes, one idea: you do the driving. The ATV is the most direct way to see Migriño — desert, canyon, the wide riverbed and out onto the Pacific beach — and the one that works best if you've never been off-road.

We ride with a guide up front setting the pace and another closing the group, so nobody gets left behind or feels rushed.
atv.note: Drivers from 16 with photo ID. Passengers from 7.

utv.name: UTV & Can-Am
utv.tagline: Wheel, belts and roll cage: from family-friendly to extreme
utv.intro:
Four machines for four different riders. The Side by Side for couples or riding with a child, the Can-Am X3 when you want real speed, the 195-horsepower Maverick for experienced drivers, and the Mini RZR so kids can drive their own.

All of them have a steering wheel, two belted seats and a roll cage. More stable and more comfortable than an ATV.
utv.note: The second seat costs nothing extra on any machine in this category.

combo.name: Combos
combo.tagline: Two or three activities in a single outing
combo.intro:
Instead of coming back a second day and paying for two transfers, you do an hour of each activity in one outing. The most requested pairing is ATV plus camel, but you build your own.

It works out considerably cheaper than booking separately, and since everything happens in one place you lose no time to transfers. It's the favorite among cruise passengers.
combo.note: The Balandra Combo is different: a full day with Balandra Beach and La Paz.

bike.name: Bikes
bike.tagline: The desert without an engine, in silence
bike.intro:
Two options depending on how hard you want to work: the electric bike, which handles the climbs for you, and the mountain bike, for anyone who actually wants to pedal.

Same desert, riverbed and beach route as the motorized tours, but hearing the desert instead of an engine. It's the cheapest way to see Migriño and the best for spotting wildlife.
bike.note: From age 12. It's also the most affordable category in the catalogue.

camel.name: Camel Ride
camel.tagline: A guided walk through desert and beach, from age 5
camel.intro:
Our camels live in a sanctuary registered with SEMARNAT and walk at their own pace, always with a handler on foot. This isn't a speed tour: it's about the landscape, the photos and time with the animals.

It's what works best with small children and grandparents, and easily what generates the most photos from the trip.
camel.note: From age 5. No previous experience needed.

horse.name: Horseback Ride
horse.tagline: An easy trot facing the Pacific waves
horse.intro:
Gentle horses, a guide beside you the whole way, and a route that runs from the desert straight to the shoreline. You don't need to know how to ride: we set the pace to the group.

It's the calmest tour we run, and by far the best one at sunset.

skybike.name: Sky Bikes
skybike.intro:
A fixed bicycle on a cable strung from one side of the canyon to the other. You sit and pedal at your own pace, in a double harness with an independent safety line.

There's no free fall and no speed: it's height and views. That's why it works for anyone who wants the scenery without the adrenaline of a traditional zipline.
skybike.note: From age 8, minimum height 1.20 m and maximum weight 120 kg.

safety: Phones, cameras and any electronic device stay put away while the activity runs. The one exception is a hands-free camera such as a GoPro, which you're welcome to bring.
Everything happens outdoors with the group in motion. The rule is there to look after you and everyone around you, and so you ride the trail instead of watching it through a screen.
The rule doesn't apply on a private tour: bring your phone and your camera, since there's no other group to affect.
The ocean along this beach is genuinely dangerous and not swimmable: rip currents, heavy surf and an uneven bottom.
Every beach in Mexico is public, but inside the property nobody goes in the water at any point, before or after your activity.
Anyone who chooses to enter the ocean does so at their own risk, and releases the company, its owners, employees, affiliates and partners from any liability for injury, accident, loss or death.
How it's enforced: anyone who goes in the water has their tour ended on the spot with no refund, is driven back whenever staff decide, and cannot join any other activity that day.
